chunks: And you are free to live upon it, --

key_terms.الْبَلَدِ: The land/city (often referring to Mecca or a specific sacred place)
key_terms.حِلٌّ: Free from blame or guilt; permissible

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'And you are free from blame in this land' mean in Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase 'And you are free from blame in this city' (Makkah) is often linked to the divine protection of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the sanctity of the Kaaba, emphasizing that God is absolved of any defect in granting pardon within this sacred precinct. It highlights the unique spiritual status of Makkah as a place where divine mercy is particularly manifest, reinforcing the concept of 'Hillan' (freedom from blame) as a specific attribute of the Divine in relation to the sacred geography.
